title: The Burning Sigil Anew
premise: Beatrix Thornbury has survived five years in the walled city of Vellamere by being useful and unremarkable: tasting the regent's food, dosing themselves with harmless poisons, and selling tiny charms to neighbors who pretend not to believe in magic. When the border wards collapse and the stars vanish on the same night, the country of Caelmere is revealed to have been erased from every map and memory beyond its walls—and the moon begins a thirteenth turn that will finish the erasure. Beatrix joins a ragged band of fellow 'unregistered' people, including a disgraced cartographer and a child who remembers the old sky, to find the Doorway that once led out. In the end Beatrix must choose between restoring Caelmere as it was or letting it dissolve into something new, sacrificing their own recorded past so their found family can carry its memory forward.
about_author: Rosalind Villalobos is a former pastry chef turned novelist who writes about kitchens, borders, and the quiet magic of ordinary work. She lives near the sea with her partner, two opinionated cats, and a garden that refuses to grow anything but rosemary.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A day in the regent's kitchens: tasting, dosing, and slipping charms into bread baskets for desperate customers. Establishes Beatrix's careful invisibility and their secret ledger of small magics. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Thirteen Bells
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The night bells ring thirteen times; the stars go out one by one while Beatrix stands on a rooftop watching. The border wards flare and die. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread as the familiar city becomes uncanny.

chapters.title: The Map That Forgot Us
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile Ferrant, a cartographer stripped of her license years ago, discovers her maps of Caelmere have gone blank at the borders. She seeks out rumors of an unregistered charm-seller. Emotional beat: professional shame meeting reluctant hope.

chapters.title: Neighbors Who Pretend
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Customers arrive not for charms but for answers; Beatrix denies knowing anything until a neighbor's child, Pip, draws the old constellations from memory—stars no one else recalls. Emotional beat: the cost of staying invisible when others are afraid.

chapters.title: What the Regent Knows
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Summoned before Regent Casimir, Beatrix tastes a dish laced with something that tastes like forgetting. The regent hints he bargained away the country's name long ago. Emotional beat: terror and the first crack in Beatrix's loyalty to the crown.

chapters.title: The Unregistered
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. Odile finds Beatrix through Pip's drawing; they gather others marked by the falling wards—a hedge-healer, a bell-ringer, a soldier who deserted the night the stars died. Emotional beat: wary strangers recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Magics
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix burns their charm-ledger to protect the group, then regrets it—each entry was a memory of someone helped. Pip offers to remember them aloud instead. Emotional beat: grief for a hidden life, and the first act of found family.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn Begins
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Astronomers confirm the moon has entered an impossible thirteenth phase; scholars calculate the country has until the turn completes. Odile reveals the legend of the Doorway beneath the Salt Cathedral. Emotional beat: a deadline made visible in the sky.

chapters.title: Road Through the Pale Fields
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The company leaves Vellamere through farmland where crops grow gray and tasteless—Beatrix alone can still taste them, a clue that magic is draining toward the capital. Emotional beat: leaving safety behind, homesickness on the road.

chapters.title: The Soldier's Confession
chapters.summary: Dain's POV. Dain admits he was ordered to open a ward-gate the night the stars went out and refused too late. Beatrix chooses mercy over anger. Emotional beat: guilt shared is guilt halved; trust deepens.

chapters.title: Salt Cathedral
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Beneath the ruined cathedral they find the Doorway—a stone arch covered in sigils, cold and locked. The sigil matches the brand on Beatrix's childhood memory: tasters are chosen from bloodlines once bound to the wards. Emotional beat: Beatrix's identity upended.

chapters.title: A Kitchen in Exile
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A quiet chapter: the group camps, cooks, and tells stories. Beatrix teaches Pip to bake; Odile sketches a map of a country only they remember. Emotional beat: belonging discovered in the ordinary, mid-crisis.

chapters.title: Casimir's Hunters
chapters.summary: Dain's POV. The regent's wardens ambush them; the hedge-healer Maren is captured buying time. They learn Casimir intends to feed the Doorway the last of Caelmere's magic to preserve his own rule. Emotional beat: fury and resolve; stakes become personal.

chapters.title: The Price of Names
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. An old ward-ghost in a wayshrine explains the bargain: Caelmere traded its name for protection, and the protection has expired. To reopen the Doorway, someone must offer a true name freely given. Emotional beat: understanding the sacrifice to come.

chapters.title: Rescue at the Wardenhouse
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Imprisoned, Maren resists interrogation by healing her captors' headaches until they soften. The company infiltrates; Beatrix uses taster's knowledge of poisons to disable the garrison without killing. Emotional beat: Maren learning she is worth rescuing.

chapters.title: What the Stars Remembered
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Pip dreams the old sky and wakes able to point the way to a second sigil-site. The group realizes memory itself is the counter-magic to erasure. Emotional beat: the smallest member becomes essential; wonder restored.

chapters.title: Return to Vellamere
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. They sneak back into the capital as the moon nears full thirteenth phase; the city is graying at the edges, streets literally fading. Beatrix visits the kitchen one last time. Emotional beat: farewell to the life that kept them safe and small.

chapters.title: The Regent's Bargain
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Confronting Casimir in the throne room, Beatrix learns he gave his own name decades ago and has been hollow ever since—he wants the Doorway sealed forever so no one suffers as he did. Emotional beat: pity replacing hatred; the antagonist humanized.

chapters.title: Sigil Anew
chapters.summary: All POVs interwoven. At the Doorway, the company re-inscribes the burning sigil using memories spoken aloud—every charm sold, every meal cooked, every star Pip remembers. Emotional beat: collective courage; the climax ignites.

chapters.title: A Name Freely Given
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The Doorway demands a true name. Beatrix offers theirs—not to escape but to anchor Caelmere's memory in the world beyond, accepting that no record of them will remain. Emotional beat: self-sacrifice transformed into gift.

chapters.title: The Country That Remembers Itself
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The wards rebirth rather than restore: Caelmere reappears changed, its borders open, its magic legal again. The stars return slightly wrong—new constellations shaped like the company's stories. Emotional beat: bittersweet triumph.

chapters.title: Tasting the First Morning
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Nameless but remembered by choice, Beatrix opens a bakery-teahouse where charms are sold openly beside the bread. Pip sets a place for them at the table; Odile hangs a map with a blank space lovingly labeled 'Beatrix.' Emotional beat: belonging without a name—the found family holds.
